svg.title: Engle-Granger vs Johansen
svg.desc: Engle-Granger assumes a single relation and tests residual stationarity; Johansen determines how many cointegrating relations the system has through sequential tests.
svg.text: A two-step test on one residual vs a likelihood test on the whole system
Step 2: unit root test on residuals
Swap the dependent variable and the conclusion shifts
Residual critical values differ from ADF
The size of the eigenvalues tells the number of relations
Eigenvectors are the cointegrating vectors β
Two steps and you are done
y2 = a + b·y1 + u — b is the hedge ratio
ADF on û — stationary means cointegrated
Regress Δy on û(t−1) to get α
Simple, but it assumes a single relation
The first failure to reject gives r — here r = 1
Engle-Granger assumes one relation and asks whether the residual is stationary.
Johansen asks how many relations the system has — with three or more variables, use it.
Next: handling a nonstationary VAR on a single sheet.
